outcomes.title: Opening Depot shows the natural-language prompt as the dominant element on the landing page; the workspace section grid is no longer the primary content, and every workspace/module remains reachable from the home in no more clicks than a secondary navigation path.

The home shows a prioritized feed containing approvals, exceptions, tasks, agent proposals awaiting approval and anomalies relevant to the signed-in user; items can be acted on from the feed, with one-click actions offered only where the action is safe, and anything else opens the item for review.

A user can ask a plain-language question about business data and receive an answer that cites its sources and lets them drill through to the underlying records, using the existing read-only copilot; answers never include data the user is not permitted to see.

A user can state a task in plain language and the assistant navigates to the right place, pre-fills the form, or proposes an action; any action that posts or touches money is not executed until the user explicitly approves it under approve_before_commit; the user can decline or edit the proposal.

A keyboard shortcut opens a global command bar on every page; from it a user can search navigation, look up records, and send an assistant prompt, and it is fully operable by keyboard and screen reader.
On module pages a user can invoke explain this record, what changed, and what should I do next, and receive an answer grounded in that record's data and history.

Users receive a briefing (e.g. daily) summarizing changes, risks and recommended actions drawn from ap_coding, cash_application, mrp_triage, collections_outreach and journal_anomaly output; recommended actions link into the governed approval flow.

Each AI suggestion shows why it was made and what data it used; users can undo (where reversible) or decline it; admins can use the kill switch and set budgets; when AI is down, killed or budget-stopped, the home and navigation fall back to the classic experience and every ERP process can still be completed manually.
The home content and ordering differ by user role/duties and recent activity, and users can pin items that persist across sessions.
A first-time user sees an onboarding introduction to the AI-first experience that can be skipped and revisited later.
